````markdown
# A1: 
根据你现在的项目状态，我建议把下一阶段理解成：**Claude Code 继续作为“平台开发 agent”，但 KCA 平台本身逐步内建自己的 event log、issue/PR 协作入口、agent/skill 包管理、runtime worker 和 model router。** 你已经有很多正确实践了，接下来重点是把这些实践产品化、可审计化、可迁移化。

---

## 1. Claude Code 能否自动把 session 对话和操作日志记录到项目 `logs/xxx.md`？

**部分支持，但需要你自己用 hooks / export 脚本落地。**

Claude Code 官方会持续保存 session，本地 transcript 默认在：

```text
~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl
```

也可以在会话里用 `/export` 把当前 conversation 保存为纯文本文件；官方文档还说明这些本地 session 文件默认 30 天后清理，可通过配置调整。([Claude Code][1])

但是，**Claude Code 默认不会自动把完整对话保存到当前 repo 的 `logs/` 目录**。要做到这一点，推荐用 hooks。Claude Code hooks 能在 `SessionStart`、`UserPromptSubmit`、`PreToolUse`、`PostToolUse`、`Stop`、`SubagentStart/Stop`、`TaskCreated/Completed`、`SessionEnd` 等生命周期事件触发；hook 输入里包含 `session_id`、`cwd`、`transcript_path` 等信息。([Claude Code][2])

你项目里其实已经有一个基础版本：`audit_event.py` 会从 hook stdin 读取 JSON payload，然后写到当前项目的 `.agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl`，字段包括 `timestamp`、`hook_event_name`、`tool_name`、`session_id`、`cwd` 和完整 payload。 这说明你的项目已经具备 **tool-event audit log**，但还没有完整的 **conversation transcript mirror / session summary log**。

我建议分三层做：

```text
.agent/audit/
  tool-events.jsonl              # raw hook events, 默认不提交或只提交 sanitized 样例

logs/claude-sessions/
  <date>-<session-id>.jsonl       # transcript mirror，可选，不建议默认 commit
  <date>-<session-id>.summary.md  # curated session summary，可 review 后 commit

docs/handoffs/
  m9-handoff.md
  m10-handoff.md                  # milestone 级别核心记忆，应该 commit
```

关键安全建议：**不要默认把完整 transcript commit 到 GitHub**。Claude session 里可能包含本地路径、命令输出、错误日志、环境变量片段、PR 链接、甚至误打印的 secret。更好的做法是：

```text
raw logs:
  .agent/audit/**
  logs/claude-sessions/raw/**
  默认 .gitignore

curated memory:
  PROJECT_STATE.md
  docs/handoffs/*.md
  docs/adr/*.md
  docs/meeting-notes/*.md
  docs/evidence/*.md
  review 后 commit
```

可以让 Claude Code 加一个 skill：

```text
.claude/skills/session-closeout/SKILL.md
```

用途是每次长任务结束后生成：

```text
- What changed
- Files changed
- Tests run
- Decisions made
- Open questions
- Follow-up issues to create
- Memory updates proposed
```

然后由 human 批准后更新 `PROJECT_STATE.md`、`docs/handoffs/`、ADR 或 GitHub issue。

## 2. Claude Code 支持 GitHub webhook 吗？能否响应 PR review / comments / labels？

**支持几种不同层级，但要区分 “GitHub Actions 触发新 agent run” 和 “push 事件进入正在运行的本地 session”。**

### 方案 A：GitHub Actions + `@claude`，最稳

你现在已经有 `.github/workflows/claude.yml`，它监听：

```yaml
issue_comment:
  types: [created]
pull_request_review_comment:
  types: [created]
issues:
  types: [opened, assigned]
pull_request_review:
  types: [submitted]
```

并且只有 comment / issue / review body 包含 `@claude` 时才运行 Claude Code Action。 官方文档也确认 Claude Code GitHub Actions 可以通过 PR/issue 中的 `@claude` 触发，分析代码、创建 PR、实现功能和修 bug，并且 action 是基于 Claude Agent SDK 构建的。([Claude Code][3])

这适合：

```text
@claude review this PR
@claude implement issue #123
@claude summarize unresolved review comments
@claude update docs based on this decision
```

如果你想让它更新 issue comments / labels / PR comments，workflow 权限需要从 read 扩到 write，例如：

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read
  id-token: write
```

但我建议分 workflow：

```text
claude.yml
  手动 @claude 响应，允许 contents/pull-requests/issues write

claude-code-review.yml
  自动 PR review，默认只读或只写 review comment

issue-triage.yml
  label/comment triage，issues: write，但不改代码

labels-sync.yml
  只同步 .github/labels.yml，需要人工 workflow_dispatch
```

工程实践文档里的 AI pickup rule 很适合这里：implementation agent 只能处理 open issue、带 `ai:ready`、决策已 `decision:confirmed`、有 acceptance criteria、无 `ai:blocked`，且不涉及 secrets/破坏性 migration/生产 infra/客户可见副作用，除非 human 明确批准。

### 方案 B：Claude Code Routines + GitHub trigger，云端事件触发

Claude Code Routines 支持 schedule、API trigger、GitHub event trigger，运行在 Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure；GitHub trigger 会在匹配事件发生时启动一个新 session。([Claude Code][4]) 官方文档说明 GitHub triggers 当前支持 PR 和 release 两类事件，PR 事件包括 opened、closed、assigned、labeled、synchronized 等；每个匹配事件都会启动独立 session，不复用之前的 session。([Claude Code][4])

这适合：

```text
PR labeled ai:ready → 新 cloud session 生成 plan
PR updated → 自动 review diff
release created → 生成 release notes / readiness report
nightly → issue backlog grooming
```

但它不适合保存“一个长期本地 session 的连续上下文”，因为每个 GitHub event 是新 session。你的 repo memory 仍然要靠 GitHub 文件和 issue/PR 记录。

### 方案 C：Claude Code Channels，把 webhook 推进正在运行的本地 session

Claude Code Channels 是另一类东西：它允许 MCP server 把 messages、alerts、webhooks 推入一个正在运行的 Claude Code session。官方说它可用于 CI results、chat messages、monitoring events，让 Claude 在你离开终端时也能反应；这是 research preview，需要 Claude Code v2.1.80+，并且 session 启动时要用 `--channels` opt-in。([Claude Code][5]) Channels reference 说明 channel 本质是 MCP server，通过 `notifications/claude/channel` 把外部事件送进 Claude Code session，可做 one-way webhook 或 two-way chat bridge。([Claude Code][6])

这适合：

```text
GitHub webhook → local channel server → active Arch Claude session
CI failed → Claude sees event immediately
Issue label changed → Claude receives payload
PR review submitted → Claude receives payload and responds
```

但它更复杂，且是 research preview。我建议你的路线是：

```text
短期：
  GitHub Actions @claude + issue labels/comments

中期：
  Routines 处理 cloud-side GitHub event automation

高级：
  Channels 将 selected GitHub webhook 推入正在运行的 Arch session
```

## 3. 如何从 GitHub comments 中提取需求确认/设计变更并沉淀为核心记忆？

这件事不能让 Claude “看到评论就直接改 PROJECT_STATE”。应该用 **两阶段 memory promotion**：

```text
GitHub comment/review/label event
  ↓
Issue Triage / Decision Extractor agent
  ↓
生成 proposed memory patch
  ↓
human review
  ↓
更新核心记忆文件
```

我建议新增这些文件：

```text
.claude/agents/github-decision-extractor.md
.claude/agents/github-issue-triage.md
.claude/agents/pr-review-followup.md

.claude/skills/github-comment-distill/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/memory-promotion/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/pr-closeout-review/SKILL.md
```

`github-comment-distill` 的职责：

```text
输入：
  issue/PR comments, review comments, labels, PR diff, linked task doc

输出：
  confirmed_requirements:
  changed_requirements:
  confirmed_design_decisions:
  changed_design_decisions:
  open_questions:
  blockers:
  proposed_labels:
  proposed_core_memory_patch:
```

`memory-promotion` 的职责：

```text
只生成 patch，不直接 claim truth：
- PROJECT_STATE.md patch
- docs/adr/xxxx.md draft
- docs/tasks/Mx-Txxx.md update
- docs/handoffs/mx-handoff.md update
- GitHub issue comment summary
```

沉淀规则建议：

```text
comment 只是 evidence，不自动成为 truth
label decision:confirmed + human 明确 wording 才能进入 ADR / PROJECT_STATE
模糊评论 → decision:needed + ai:blocked
实现细节 → task doc / PR closeout
长期架构决策 → ADR
milestone 状态 → PROJECT_STATE / docs/milestones.md
```

这和你的工程实践文档一致：Issue Triage Agent 可以读 comments 并识别问题是否已解决，但不能从模糊评论推断决策；Implementation Agent 只能在确认后的 issue 上工作。

## 4. agents/skills 如何迁移到别的项目？

**不要直接无脑复制到目标项目根目录。最佳方式是“staging → audit → adapt → install”。**

Claude Code skills 是文件系统 artifact，项目级 skills 放在：

```text
.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
```

个人级 skills 放在：

```text
~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
```

官方文档说明 project skills 只对当前项目生效，personal skills 对所有项目生效，plugin skills 通过 plugin namespace 生效；skills 的 body 只在使用时加载，适合把重复流程从 `CLAUDE.md` 中拆出来。([Claude Code][7]) Agent SDK 也支持从 `.claude/skills/`、`~/.claude/skills/` 或 plugin 路径发现 filesystem skills。([Claude Code][8])

我建议采用四层复用模型：

### A. 通用、无项目耦合：做成 personal skill 或内部 plugin

例如：

```text
pr-closeout-review
github-comment-distill
session-closeout
ci-failure-triage
test-coverage-review
```

可以放：

```text
~/.claude/skills/
```

或建立一个内部 repo：

```text
kca-agent-pack/
  skills/
  agents/
  hooks/
  templates/
  README.md
```

然后每个项目通过 submodule/subtree 或脚本安装。

### B. 项目相关但可复用：先放 staging

目标项目里先放：

```text
.agent-import-staging/kca-agent-pack/
```

然后让 Claude Code 执行：

```text
Analyze .agent-import-staging/kca-agent-pack.
For each skill/agent:
- classify as reusable / needs adaptation / reject
- identify project-specific assumptions
- identify commands, paths, labels, policies to rewrite
- propose final installation path
Do not install until plan is approved.
```

再迁移到：

```text
.claude/skills/
.claude/agents/
docs/agent-practices/
```

### C. 强项目耦合：不要迁移，只迁移理念

例如 KCA 专用的 Kaggle approval、competition artifact layout、Supabase schema agent，不适合直接复制到普通 SaaS 项目。应该抽象出：

```text
approval-gate-review
artifact-ledger
remote-side-effect-policy
```

### D. 带脚本的 skills：必须安全审计

官方 Agent Skills 文档提醒，Skills 可以包含指令和代码，恶意 Skill 可能诱导 Claude 执行不符合预期的工具或代码，所以只应使用可信来源的 skills。([Claude Platform][9]) 所以迁移时要检查：

```text
- 是否调用 curl/wget/bash remote code
- 是否读取 .env / ssh / cloud credentials
- 是否 git push / deploy / delete
- 是否写绝对路径
- 是否假设某个 repo layout
- 是否修改 permissions/hooks
```

## 5. 产品 release 后是否还依赖 Claude Code？agents/skills/commands 底层调用什么？

**KCA 产品 release 后不应该依赖 Claude Code CLI/desktop 本身。** Claude Code 是开发工具；KCA runtime 应该是你自己的 platform worker。

你现在项目文档已经把两类 agent 区分得很清楚：Claude Code/VS Code/Desktop/Web 是 platform-development coding agents；runtime competition code agents 是平台内部启动的 agent，初始方向是 Claude Agent SDK、隔离 workspace/container、Kaggle Python/notebook-first、未来 model router 支持 Claude、GPT-style、local vLLM/Ollama 等。

更进一步，你当前 M3 里已经把 runtime agent 方向改成了 provider-agnostic：`litellm.completion()` 作为统一 LLM provider interface，Claude、GPT-4o、本地 vLLM/Ollama 可按 job 选择。 这说明 KCA runtime **不是锁死在 Anthropic 模型上**。

不过要分清楚几种能力来源：

```text
Claude Code CLI skills/agents/hooks:
  用于开发 KCA repo；依赖 Claude Code。

KCA .kca/skills or tools:
  你自己定义的产品 runtime skills/tools；不依赖 Claude Code。

Claude Agent SDK:
  可以作为一种 runtime harness，提供 Claude Code-like agent loop、工具执行、context management。

LiteLLM / OpenAI-compatible / vLLM / Ollama:
  可以作为 model provider；你要自己实现 tool loop 或通过 KCA worker adapter 接入。

KCA commands:
  例如 kca run, kca decision, kca kaggle, kca skill；
  release 后就是你的产品 CLI/runtime API，不应该依赖 Claude Code。
```

官方 Claude Agent SDK 的定位是“把 Claude Code 作为 library 构建生产 AI agents”，它提供相同的 tools、agent loop、context management，并且适合 CI/CD、custom applications、production automation。([Claude Code][10]) 但如果你使用 Agent SDK，它主要还是 Claude/Anthropic provider 体系；如果要接 vLLM/Ollama/OpenAI，你需要通过 KCA 的 model router / LiteLLM 路线来承接。

我的建议：

```text
产品 runtime 层：
  KCA Worker API
    - job runner
    - permission policy
    - tool executor
    - audit/event log
    - model router
    - GitHub adapter
    - Kaggle adapter

可插拔 agent backend：
  - Claude Agent SDK backend
  - LiteLLM tool-loop backend
  - OpenAI Responses/Codex backend
  - Local vLLM/Ollama backend
```

这样你可以先用 Claude Agent SDK 获得强 agentic coding 能力，后面逐步替换或混合其他模型。

## 6. 如何让 Claude Code 在 plan/design/architect 阶段更主动发现问题、提问和 debate？

你观察得很对：Claude Code 有时会“按字面完成任务”，不会主动追问隐藏需求。例如你让它接手 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml`，它没有主动发现“多 Kaggle 账户提交”这种重要历史设计理念。其实你的 legacy 工具里已经有不少信号：`kkr.py` 支持 `--env` 覆盖 selected owner 的 dotenv path，`RunManifest` 里有 `owner`、`slug`、`env_path`，`kkr.yaml` 里也出现多个 Kaggle owner/kernel id，例如 `harrysun2006`、`firefly2006`。  

要提高主动性，我建议建立一个 **Discovery / Debate Gate**，不是只靠“plan mode”。

### 做法 1：每个迁移 legacy 的任务先跑 “design archaeology”

新增 skill：

```text
.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md
```

要求 Claude 在实现前必须输出：

```text
Legacy design archaeology:
1. What workflows does the legacy tool support?
2. What hidden assumptions exist?
3. What user personas/accounts exist?
4. What side effects exist?
5. What state files/registries exist?
6. What config dimensions exist?
7. Which features should be preserved?
8. Which features should be deprecated?
9. What questions must be asked before implementation?
10. What tests prove behavior parity?
```

对 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml` 这种任务，强制它先识别：

```text
- multi-account / owner / env mapping
- kernel push vs competition submit
- notebook submit vs local file submit
- run registry
- version labels
- fetch/watch/status/list lifecycle
- dry-run behavior
- H100 / docker_image / Kaggle metadata patch notes
```

### 做法 2：在 task template 里加入 “assumption challenge”

每个 architecture task 的 prompt 里固定加：

```text
Before proposing implementation, challenge the task:
- What important requirement might be hidden in legacy files?
- What would break for an expert user?
- What design questions should be asked?
- What should be preserved even if not mentioned?
- What is the minimal reversible implementation?
- Give at least 3 alternative designs and argue tradeoffs.
```

### 做法 3：增加反方 agent

新增 agents：

```text
.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md
.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md
.claude/agents/design-red-team.md
```

`requirements-skeptic` 不写代码，只问问题。
`legacy-archaeologist` 只读 legacy scripts/configs，提取设计理念。
`design-red-team` 反驳当前方案，指出丢失能力和长期成本。

### 做法 4：把“询问 human”变成 acceptance criteria

例如：

```text
Acceptance criteria:
- The agent identified at least 5 legacy behavior dimensions.
- The agent listed preserved / changed / dropped behaviors.
- The agent asked human for unresolved design decisions unless all are explicitly answered by docs/tests.
- No implementation starts until hidden assumptions are documented.
```

这比“请主动一点”有效，因为它把主动性变成可检查输出。

## 7. 你现在这些实践之外，还能怎么提高开发效率和准确率？

你已经有一套很强的 workflow：

```text
milestones/tasks + worktrees
Arch Linux Claude Code --bg 长跑
Mac VS Code 做短任务/review
mobile app remote control 批准/回答
GitHub issues/PR/comments/labels 作为第二交互界面
```

我建议补齐下面 12 个实践。

### 1. 给每个 task 增加 “evidence bundle”

每个 PR 必须产出：

```text
docs/evidence/<task-id>/
  closeout.md
  commands-run.txt
  test-results.md
  screenshots-or-traces-index.md
  decisions.md
```

PR body 链接 evidence。工程实践文档也建议 logs 要总结到 issue，并把长期证据放在 `docs/evidence/` 或 GitHub artifact 中。

### 2. 建立 “no silent memory” 机制

每次 Claude Code 结束时强制问：

```text
Does this task change project memory?
- no
- yes: propose patch to PROJECT_STATE.md / ADR / task doc / handoff
```

只有 human approve 后才更新。

### 3. 增加 PR Closeout bot

每个 PR 自动检查：

```text
- linked issue
- acceptance criteria checked
- tests run
- docs updated or not needed
- migrations/RLS/secrets impact
- remote side effects
- evidence link
```

你的 engineering details 里已经建议 `pr-closeout-check.yml` 用于检查 PR body 是否包含 tests/docs/inventory/closeout links。

### 4. 将 “labels” 变成状态机，而不只是标签

建议状态流：

```text
ai:triage
  → decision:needed + ai:blocked
  → decision:confirmed
  → ai:ready
  → ai:implementing
  → PR opened
  → review
  → merged / follow-up issues
```

禁止：

```text
ai:ready + decision:needed
ai:ready + ai:blocked
ai:implementing without owner/branch
```

### 5. 引入 “issue-to-branch naming convention”

例如：

```text
issue #123
branch: claude/issue-123-short-title
worktree: .worktrees/issue-123-short-title
PR title: [#123] Short title
```

这样 GitHub event、Claude session、worktree、logs、evidence 都能对齐。

### 6. 为 Claude Code session 命名

Claude Code 支持命名、resume、branch session；session picker 可以按当前 repo/worktree/branch 查找，并且可以导出 transcript。([Claude Code][1]) 你的长跑命令应统一：

```bash
claude --bg \
  --name "M9-T002-spaceship-baseline-issue-123" \
  ...
```

然后 log/evidence 也用同名 ID。

### 7. 用 Channels 或 Remote Control 做“响应式开发”，但不要替代 GitHub Actions

Remote Control 适合你现在用 mobile app 远程接管本地 session；官方说明 Remote Control 让本地 Claude Code session 继续运行在你的机器上，Web/mobile 只是窗口，适合从手机继续本地任务。([Claude Code][11])

Channels 更适合把外部 webhook 推入本地 session。我的建议：

```text
Remote Control:
  人主动介入、批准、回答问题。

GitHub Actions:
  repo-native 事件、@claude、issue/PR 协作。

Channels:
  高级事件流，例如 CI failed / PR labeled / issue assigned 推入正在跑的 Arch session。
```

### 8. 让 KCA 自己 dogfood GitHub interface

KCA 产品本身未来要能操作 GitHub，所以现在开发 KCA 时就用同一套抽象：

```text
GitHub issue/comment/label event
  → KCA event adapter
  → decision extractor
  → job queue
  → worker/session
  → PR/comment/label update
  → audit log
```

这样你不是“额外做 GitHub automation”，而是在 dogfood 产品核心能力。

### 9. legacy migration 要有 behavior parity tests

对 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml`，不要只迁移代码。要建立：

```text
tests/fixtures/kkr/
  kkr.yaml
  minimal_notebook.ipynb
  fake_kaggle_api.json

tests/test_kkr_parity.py
```

覆盖：

```text
- push --dry-run
- submit --dry-run
- watch/status/list/fetch parsing
- multi-owner env selection
- notebook vs local submit
- version label / registry behavior
```

`kkr.py` 已经有 dry-run、JSON output、本地 registry、watch/status/list/fetch 等能力，适合做 parity suite。

### 10. 对高风险任务使用双 agent review

例如：

```text
Agent A: implement
Agent B: review only
Agent C: test coverage reviewer
Human: final decision
```

工程实践文档本身已经把 Inventory Drift Auditor、Issue Triage Agent、Implementation Planner、Implementation Agent、Milestone Reviewer、Test Coverage Reviewer、Release Readiness Agent 分成不同职责，并规定各自不能越权。

### 11. 给 runtime worker 增加 replay

每个 job 都能：

```bash
kca job replay <job_id> --from-event <n> --dry-run
```

这样当 agent 做错时，你可以复现：

```text
input prompt
model/provider
tools allowed
tool calls
policy decisions
files changed
test results
human decisions
```

M7 的目标里已经有 “permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny” 和 “audit log records every tool execution with policy decision”。 建议把它升级成可 replay 的 event sourcing。

### 12. 明确 M9 前的 readiness gate

你的 milestones 里 M9 是第一次真实 Kaggle end-to-end regression：Spaceship Titanic，目标是通过审批 gate 执行一次真实 `kaggle competitions submit` 并记录 public LB score。 所以 M9 前一定要 gate：

```text
- CI green
- dry-run path green
- Kaggle credentials verified without printing
- submission.csv schema validated
- approval gate manually tested
- rollback / stop criteria documented
- logs/evidence path confirmed
```

Design a safe GitHub event and session-memory hardening layer for KCA development and future KCA runtime dogfooding.

Questions to answer before implementation:
1. How should Claude Code session transcripts/tool events be mirrored or summarized into project logs without committing secrets?
2. How should GitHub issue/PR comments, reviews, and labels become a human/AI collaboration interface?
3. Which comments can become core memory, and which require human confirmation?
4. Which new agents/skills are needed?
5. How should reusable agents/skills be packaged for migration to other projects?
6. How should legacy tools like kkr.py/kkr.yaml be analyzed so hidden requirements such as multi-Kaggle-account support are not missed?

Required plan sections:
- Scope
- Non-goals
- Proposed files
- Security model
- Memory promotion workflow
- GitHub event workflow
- Agent/skill list with responsibilities and Must Not rules
- Tests/smoke checks
- Rollout order
- Risks and approval gates

Important rules:
- Do not read or print secrets.
- Do not run real Kaggle submit/kernel push/upload.
- Do not make GitHub write operations without approval.
- Do not modify production Supabase.
- Do not commit raw Claude transcripts by default.
- Treat GitHub repo files as the source of truth, not hidden AI memory.

## 总结建议

你现在的方向是对的，但下一步要把“经验性流程”固化成产品机制：

```text
Claude Code 开发侧：
  hooks + session closeout + GitHub Actions/Routines/Channels + agents/skills

KCA runtime 侧：
  event log + model router + GitHub adapter + approval gate + replay + evidence bundle

共同核心：
  GitHub repo 是 source of truth
  raw logs 不等于 memory
  human-confirmed decisions 才进入 PROJECT_STATE / ADR / milestones
```

最优先做的不是 M9 继续堆功能，而是 **M8.6：session memory、GitHub event interface、legacy design archaeology、agent/skill reuse packaging**。这会直接提高后续 M9/M10 的开发效率和准确率。
````

> Located at `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md`. Key rules:
> 
> 1. **Sequencing:** Loop Prompts execute in order; each must PASS before next; failures retry only that prompt.
> 2. **Side-effects:** No real Anthropic/Kaggle API outside designated paths; default `--dry-run`; no production Supabase changes.
> 3. **Database:** Use local `supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`); DB calls need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
> 4. **Reporting:** Report PASS/FAIL/SKIP inline per prompt; write closeout format at milestone end.
> 5. **Git/GitHub (worktree mode):** Mid-milestone: stage only, no commit. At end: `git add` closeout files, one commit per Loop Prompt (or squash), `git push` worktree branch, `gh pr create` against `main` using final-review as body.
> 6. **Secrets denied always:** `.env*`, `kaggle.json`, `~/.ssh/*`, `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`, `secrets/**`.

```markdown
# Kaggle Code Agent — Project State

_Last updated: 2026-05-24 (M9 exit)_

## Product intent
Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, approvals, and `agent_tool_audit` (M8).
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.
7. Operator-facing UI: Dashboard, Run Timeline (OTEL swim-lane), Experiments, Research, Approval Inbox + Decision Gate, Artifact Browser.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

Mutations from the UI flow through `services/decision_api/` (FastAPI) →
`tools/kca/decisions.py` → DB. The browser bundle never holds a
Supabase service-role key. The M7 permission policy resolution stays
authoritative.
```

````markdown
# kaggle-code-agent Milestones

Status: M0–M9 done; M10 in planning (authorized CTF/lab workflow)  
Created: 2026-05-16  
Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform

## Product thesis

`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.

Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.  
Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.

The platform should help a human user:

- discuss ideas and strategies;
- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.

Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.

## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.

### 1. Platform-development coding agents

These are external AI tools used to build this repository.

Examples:

- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.

Role:

- write and review this product's source code;
- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
- run local tests and CI repair loops;
- open branches/PRs under human supervision.

Important rule: these tools do not share hidden memory reliably. GitHub repository files are the durable source of truth.

### 2. Runtime competition code agents

These are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete.

Initial runtime direction:

- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker/harness;
- isolated workspace/container per job;
- Python/notebook-first for Kaggle;
- TypeScript/Python service boundary depending on platform vs worker needs;
- future model router for Claude, GPT-style models, local vLLM/Ollama models, and specialized tools.

Runtime agents must operate under competition-specific policy, sandboxing, budget limits, approval gates, and audit logging.

## Architecture north star

```text
Human user / future UI
        ↓
TypeScript-first platform/control plane
  - project/session/job/task queue
  - policy and approval gates
  - discussion/research/analysis records
  - experiment/run/submission/artifact records
  - model router configuration
        ↓
Worker layer
  - Python-first Kaggle workers
  - Claude Agent SDK runtime sessions
  - notebooks/scripts/tools/kca wrappers
  - Playwright/browser/research tools
  - sandboxed execution and evaluation
        ↓
External systems
  - GitHub repo / branches / PRs
  - Supabase DB/storage/edge functions later
  - Kaggle API/CLI, only with approval for remote side effects
  - authorized CTF/lab/hackathon platforms under explicit policy
```

## Cross-cutting rules

- GitHub repo files are the project memory and source of truth.
- Each agent task gets a branch/worktree/PR when it modifies code.
- Main branch remains stable and protected.
- Do not allow multiple AI sessions to edit the same branch/files at the same time.
- No secrets in repo, prompts, logs, artifacts, or screenshots.
- Kaggle submissions, kernel pushes, dataset uploads, and other remote side effects require explicit human approval.
- CTF/lab work must be local/sandboxed or explicitly authorized.
- Every task prompt should include acceptance criteria and a stop condition.
- Every worker loop should have budget, turn, time, and side-effect limits.
- Tests and local validation should run before external submission.

## Milestone final-review protocol

After every milestone final review, before marking done:

1. Update `PROJECT_STATE.md` — set current milestone, summarize open decisions, and record any new known blockers.
2. Update `README.md` current milestone section to name the new active milestone and goal.
3. Update `docs/milestones.md` — mark the finished milestone `✓ done`, add a one-line summary of what landed, and note any follow-ups carried forward.
4. Write `docs/handoffs/m{x}-handoff.md` — a per-milestone, ready-to-paste context prompt for the next AI tool / session that will start M{x+1}. Use `docs/handoff-prompt.md` as the canonical template; populate the "State at handoff", "Read these files first", and "Current task" sections from the M{x} final review and the M{x+1} entry in this file. The generic `docs/handoff-prompt.md` stays as the template; the per-milestone instances live under `docs/handoffs/`.

## M6: multi-agent review + OTEL telemetry + local-model layer ✓ done

Goal: harden the M3–M5 worker with an independent reviewer agent, end-to-end
OpenTelemetry tracing, and a local-model layer that routes log-triage /
summarisation jobs to user-owned GPU hosts before paying for cloud tokens.

Planned capabilities:

- Reviewer agent (sync mode) fires before high-stakes ops
  (`kaggle_submit`, `supabase_migrate`, `git_force_push`, `dataset_upload`,
  `delete_artifact`). Verdict `approve | reject | abstain` lands in a new
  `agent_reviews` table; `approve` satisfies the matching approval gate
  without human intervention, `reject` escalates (default) or fails the
  job, `abstain` falls through to the existing human-decisions flow.
- Local-model layer (`src/worker/local_model.py`) talks to vLLM / Ollama
  endpoints on the user's GPU hosts (`snorlax` RTX 4090, `may` RTX 3090)
  via OpenAI-compatible HTTP. Numbered-slot env config
  (`KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_<n>_*`), priority ordering, a TTL-cached probe, and
  a `KCA_LOCAL_FALLBACK_MODEL` cloud fallback.
- New job types `log_triage` and `summarise` route to the local layer by
  default; `kca local probe / pick / triage` surfaces endpoint state.
- OTEL instrumentation per ADR-0007 with three exporters: stderr (dev),
  SQLite (`.agent/telemetry.sqlite`), and Supabase
  (`agent_telemetry_spans`). Spans cover job / turn / tool / reviewer /
  local-probe.
- TC-3 Spaceship Titanic exercises the reviewer-gate path end-to-end on a
  binary-classification submission flow.

## M7: KCA CLI architecture — command / skill / tool / job / permission policy ✓ done

_Shipped 2026-05-21: four-layer CLI scaffold (command/skill/tool/job), skill loader, tool registry (16 tools), three permission profiles, `kca skill list/show/run` + `kca tool list/audit/doctor`, four seed skills, audit JSONL, 15 smoke tests, and `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`. 28/28 exit checks PASS — see `docs/m7-final-review.md`._

Goal: implement the full KCA command/skill/tool/job architecture so the platform
has a stable, inspectable CLI that can drive agent workflows, replace ad-hoc
`python tools/kca/kca.py` calls, and enforce structured permission decisions.

This is distinct from the product UI shell (M8): M7 is operator/developer-facing
and headless. The UI in M8 will call into the same CLI/API surface.

See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-21-r1.md` §1–3 for full design rationale.

### Four-layer model

| Layer | Description |
|---|---|
| **Command** | Deterministic CLI/API entry points for operators (`kca job run`, `kca decision approve`). |
| **Skill** | Agent-facing workflow recipes stored under `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Callable via `kca skill run <name>` or slash-style invocation. |
| **Tool** | Executable actions with input/output schema, timeout, permission label, sandbox metadata, and audit logging. |
| **Job** | Durable records that run a skill through the agent loop with budget, turn, cost, runtime limits, and decision gates. |

### M7 task sequence

| Task | Description | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| M7-T000 | Audit + repair `.github/workflows/` — fix failing CI checks, add no-db + lint jobs | — |
| M7-T001 | Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter; argument substitution | — |
| M7-T002 | Command registry: register KCA CLI subcommands declaratively | T001 |
| M7-T003 | Tool registry: tool metadata, approval policy labels, sandbox metadata | T001 |
| M7-T004 | Permission policy layer: allow/ask/deny resolution with structured JSON policy records | T003 |
| M7-T005 | Slash-style invocation: `kca skill run <name> [args] [--dry-run]` shows permissions + rendered prompt | T001, T004 |
| M7-T006 | Audit logging: record every tool execution in `agent_job_events` with policy decision | T004 |
| M7-T007 | Seed `.kca/skills/` with `run-milestone`, `triage-log`, `prepare-submission`, `review-pr` | T001 |
| M7-T008 | `tests/test_m7_smoke.py`: skill parsing, arg substitution, permission resolution, command registry, decision gates | T001–T006 |
| M7-T009 | Documentation: `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` explaining Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs | all |
| M7-T010 | M7 exit criteria validation + `docs/m7-final-review.md` | all |

### Permission policy design

Runtime agent permissions are data, not ad-hoc prompts:

```json
{
  "operation": "kaggle.submit",
  "default_decision": "ask",
  "reason": "External competition submission",
  "allowed_in_modes": ["human-approved", "competition-finalization"],
  "audit_required": true
}
```

Allow by default: edit workspace files, run tests/benchmark, create artifacts,
summarize logs, call LiteLLM/local models, create branch, commit, create PR.

Decision gate: submit to Kaggle, merge PR, publish dataset/kernel, apply
remote Supabase migration, spend above budget threshold, change model tier,
change competition direction/objective.

Deny: read secrets, write outside workspace, sudo/root, rm outside workspace,
drop database/schema, force push, network exfiltration.

### Recommended directory layout

```text
.kca/
  skills/
    run-milestone/SKILL.md
    triage-log/SKILL.md
    prepare-submission/SKILL.md
    review-pr/SKILL.md
  tools/tools.yaml
  permissions/
    default.yaml
    permissive-dev.yaml
    competition-runner.yaml

tools/kca/
  kca.py
  commands/
    job.py  skill.py  tool.py  decision.py
    workspace.py  kaggle.py  supabase.py
  agent/
    runner.py  skill_loader.py  tool_executor.py
    permission_policy.py  audit.py

- `kca skill list` shows available skills from `.kca/skills/`.

- `kca skill run <name> ... --dry-run` prints planned tool permissions and rendered prompt without executing.
- Permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny for any (operation, mode) pair.
- Audit log records every tool execution with policy decision.
- `.github/workflows/` CI passes on main branch (no-db + lint at minimum).
- `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` passes without API keys or DB.

## M10: notebook-submission regression — Petals to the Metal

_Promoted to `ai:ready` 2026-05-24 (issue #12). Decisions confirmed:
target competition `tpu-getting-started`; ONE real kernel push under
human approval; sequenced after issue #11 (dotenv leak) for the
dry-run leg; per-milestone worktree per `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §5._

Goal: validate the full platform loop with a real Kaggle **kernel push**
(notebook submission) for
[Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/tpu-getting-started)
(multi-class image classification, public leaderboard, no cash prize,
safe for repeated dry-run + 1 real kernel push under human approval).

M9 validated the **CSV-submission** path (`kca kaggle submit` →
`kaggle competitions submit`). M10 validates the **notebook-submission**
path (`kca kaggle push` → `kaggle kernels push` + kernel-run wait + LB
record) end-to-end against a real competition. The `kernel_push`
reviewer-gate / approval-inbox round-trip gets the same regression
treatment that `kaggle_submit` got in M9-T003.

### M10 task sequence (proposed)

| Task | Description |
|---|---|
| M10-T000 | Verify Kaggle credentials + register `tpu-getting-started` in the local control plane. READ_ONLY Kaggle calls. |
| M10-T001 | Data discovery + manifest for a non-CSV competition. Record `kaggle competitions files` output; document the TFRecord-style data the kernel will read at runtime. |
| M10-T002 | Author baseline notebook (transfer learning from a pretrained ImageNet backbone); local CV / holdout score recorded via `kca run`. No kernel push yet. |
| M10-T003 | Reviewer gate fires for the `kernel_push` target_op; human approves via `kca decisions approve` (NOT via real Kaggle kernel push). |
| M10-T004 | **ONE** real `kca kaggle push` under explicit human approval. Wait for the kernel run to complete; record the resulting public LB score in the `submissions` table. |
| M10-T005 | Second experiment (different backbone or augmentation policy); local only. Second real kernel push is out of scope unless explicitly re-decided. |
| M10-T006 | Regression assertions: local CV thresholds (TBD), LB recorded, kernel-push round-trip recorded in `submissions` / `runs`. |
| M10-T007 | `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` mirroring `tests/test_m9_e2e.py`: notebook ↔ percent-format round-trip via `kg-nb`, kernel-push refusal without credentials, decision_api approval round-trip — all without real Kaggle calls. **Hard pre-req: issue #11 (dotenv leak) merged.** |
| M10-T008 | M10 exit criteria validation + `docs/m10-final-review.md`. |

Exit criteria (proposed — final list lands in `docs/m10-loop-prompts.md`):

- `tpu-getting-started` registered; data manifest recorded; baseline notebook
  authored and runs locally to a recorded CV/holdout score.
- Reviewer gate fires for `kernel_push` and records `agent_reviews` +
  `human_decisions` rows before the kernel push.
- Exactly ONE real `kca kaggle push` runs under human approval; the
  resulting kernel run completes; public LB score recorded.
- Second experiment achieves measurably higher local CV than baseline,
  or surfaces a documented reason why not.
- `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` (dry-run, no credentials) passes in CI; the
  dotenv leak from issue #11 is no longer reachable from the test
  subprocess.
- `docs/m10-final-review.md` PASS, mirroring the M8 / M8.5 / M9 layout.

Gaps this milestone is expected to close (or scope to a follow-up):

- `kca kaggle push` plumbing parity with `cmd_submit` (credentials gate,
  policy-from-env gate, refusal path).
- `kg-nb` skill notebook ↔ percent-format round-trip exercised both
  directions.
- `kernel_push` reviewer-gate wiring in `src/worker/reviewer.py`.
- Submission-format detection (related: issue #7) — natural to design
  inside M10's T001 / T002 scope if the user wants it bundled.
- Daily-limit guardrails for kernel push (related: issue #8).
````

````markdown
# M9 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Spaceship Titanic](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/spaceship-titanic/overview)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M8.5 exit confirmed (CI green + GitHub Issues/PR/labels interface in place; see `docs/m8_5-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, worktree commit/push/PR at milestone end, secret denylist)._

---

## M9 at a glance

M9 is the **first end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform. It
exercises the M3 worker, M5 research path, M6 reviewer + telemetry, the M7
permission policy, and the M8 decision_api + UI shell against a real Kaggle
competition. The competition is Spaceship Titanic — binary classification,
public leaderboard, no cash prize, safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a
single real submission under an explicit human-approval gate.

M9 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates*, not that
the LB score is high. The CV thresholds in `docs/milestones.md` §M9 are
sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M9 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M8.5-T001 (CI repair) is merged on main.
- M8.5-T002 (engineering practice + GitHub interface) is merged on main and
  `.github/labels.yml` has been synced to `origin` (33 labels visible via
  `gh label list`).
- `scripts/sync_labels.py --dry-run` reports `0 update`.
- `docs/m8_5-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M9 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates submit on presence |
| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
| Data download + checksum | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_download`, `cmd_verify` (sha256 manifest already implemented in M5) | T001 |
| Worker loop (research → baseline → CV → submission file) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
| Reviewer gate before submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox | T003 |
| Real Kaggle submit (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` + `kaggle competitions submit` | T004 — single real call |
| Second experiment (HGB / feature engineering) | same worker, second run | T005 |
| Regression assertions | `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` + `runs` table | T006 / T007 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `policy:approval-required` | every task — work order issue per task |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T008 |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
  T004's single approved call.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M9 follow-ups from M8 (multi-user auth, artifact preview via
  signed URLs, live-DB CI on fork PRs, OTEL collector wiring). Those are
  separate milestones; if M9 surfaces blockers for them, file follow-up
  issues — don't expand scope.
- Adding new CLI subcommands. M9 uses the existing `kca` surface
  (`competition`, `kaggle`, `run`, `research`, `review`, `decisions`,
  `skill`) without inventing new ones.
- Runtime submission-format detection. KCA's `kca kaggle submit` is
  format-agnostic: it passes `--file` straight to `kaggle competitions
  submit`, and Kaggle validates server-side. **M9 assumes
  `submission.csv` because Spaceship Titanic is a CSV competition.** Other
  competition shapes (code-competition notebooks → `kca kaggle push`;
  `submission.zip`; JSON; etc.) need different paths that KCA does not
  yet auto-select. Tracked as a separate `area:kaggle` / `type:feature`
  follow-up — see M9-T002's "Submission-format note" for context.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
````

````markdown
# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
  step.
- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).

## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode

This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
branched off `main`.

- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
     section (or its equivalent).
  2. `git commit` using either:
     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
     last commit.
  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.

- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
  - `git push --force` (any branch)
  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
  - any push to `main` directly
  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
    milestone

- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.

## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads

These are always denied, regardless of milestone:

- `.env*`
- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
- `secrets/**`

Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
the hook layer.

---

## How a milestone references this file

In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
one line near the top:

```
Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
```

A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:

- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).

````
</details>

```markdown
# M9-T000: Kaggle credentials + competition registration

## Milestone
M9: live end-to-end regression test — Spaceship Titanic.

## Goal
Confirm the agent can read Kaggle credentials from `.env` without exposing
them, run READ_ONLY Kaggle calls, and register Spaceship Titanic in the
local control plane. No real submit, no kernel push, no dataset/model
upload.

This task assumes **M8.5 (T001, T002, T003) is merged on main**, CI is
green, and the 33 labels from `.github/labels.yml` are synced on `origin`.

## Read first

1. `PROJECT_STATE.md`
2. `AGENTS.md`
3. `CLAUDE.md`

    are on `ask`

    are denied

1. Verify `.env` defines `KAGGLE_USERNAME` and `KAGGLE_KEY`. Do **not**
   `cat .env`, `head .env`, `awk` it, or print it. Use `python-dotenv` or
   `os.environ` after `load_dotenv()` and only assert presence
   (`bool(os.environ.get("KAGGLE_USERNAME"))`).
2. Run `kca kaggle list --json` (READ_ONLY) to confirm credentials work.
   Capture only the count or competition slugs, never the raw response.

   (LOCAL_WRITE, gated on the local DB).

   the entry is in the `competitions` table.

  existing READ_ONLY ones.

## Permissions

  per protocol §5 — overridden only by the milestone closeout).
```

```markdown
# M9-T002: Worker baseline LR loop → submission.csv

## Milestone
M9: live end-to-end regression test — Spaceship Titanic.

## Goal
Drive the M3 AgentWorker through a complete baseline experiment loop for
Spaceship Titanic: research → baseline LogisticRegression → cross-validation
→ `submission.csv`. The result is a *staged* submission file and a CV
score recorded in the `runs` table. **No** real Kaggle submission.

This task assumes **M9-T000 and M9-T001 closeouts are PASS**.

## Read first

1. M9-T001 closeout
2. `src/worker/worker.py`, `src/worker/budget.py`, `src/worker/tools.py`,
   `src/worker/reviewer.py`, `src/worker/routing.py`
3. `tools/kca/run.py` (run-init + record-metric)
4. `tools/kca/skill.py` (`kca skill run --execute`)
5. `.kca/skills/kaggle-experiment-loop/SKILL.md`
6. `supabase/migrations/0005_m5_research_citations.sql`,
   `supabase/migrations/0006_m6_reviews_spans.sql`
7. `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`

## Submission-format note

**Spaceship Titanic accepts CSV submissions only** (`PassengerId,Transported`).
The current `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` is format-agnostic — it shells
out to `kaggle competitions submit -c <slug> -f <file> -m <msg>` with the
file path verbatim, and lets the Kaggle server validate the format. KCA
does **not** read competition rules at runtime to confirm the expected
submission format or pick between `submit` (CSV / zip) and `push` (kernel
notebook).

For M9 this is acceptable because Spaceship Titanic is a CSV competition.
For other competitions (code competitions → kernels via `kca kaggle push`;
some CV competitions → `submission.zip`; some structured competitions →
JSON), the executor must know the format up front; KCA will not auto-detect.

A follow-up issue tracks adding runtime format awareness to KCA
(see `area:kaggle` / `type:feature` issues filed alongside this milestone).
That work is **not** in scope for M9-T002 or any other M9 task — M9 uses
the existing `submit` surface and assumes CSV for Spaceship Titanic.

## Scope

1. `kca run init --competition spaceship-titanic --name baseline-lr` to
   create a run artifact directory under
   `runs/spaceship-titanic/baseline-lr/`.
2. Execute the kaggle-experiment-loop skill via
   `kca skill run kaggle-experiment-loop --execute --arg metric=Accuracy`
   (or equivalent — match the skill's declared arguments).
3. Inside the worker, produce:
   - a brief research summary citing competition page + 1–2 forum
     references (M5 surface);
   - a baseline `LogisticRegression` model trained on `train.csv` with
     a deterministic CV split (seed pinned, recorded in the run meta);
   - CV accuracy recorded via `kca run record-metric` (writes to `runs`).
4. Produce `runs/spaceship-titanic/baseline-lr/submission.csv` matching
   the `sample_submission.csv` schema (`PassengerId`, `Transported`).
5. Quick sanity validation: row count == test.csv row count; columns
   match sample; values are booleans (or 0/1).

## Non-goals

- Do not call `kca kaggle submit`. The submission file is *staged* only.
- Do not push a kernel.
- Do not iterate beyond the baseline within this Loop Prompt — feature
  engineering and HGB are M9-T005.
- Do not call the real Anthropic API outside skill-declared paths; if the
  worker is run with `--dry-run`, that's acceptable — record the
  dry-run flag in the closeout.

## Acceptance criteria

- `runs/spaceship-titanic/baseline-lr/submission.csv` exists.
- A row in `runs` references the baseline run with a recorded CV metric.
- Sanity validation passes (row count, column names, value types).
- `kca run list --competition spaceship-titanic --json` shows the run.
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Append Claude Code hook events to a local JSONL audit log."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> int:
    try:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except Exception as exc:
        payload = {"parse_error": str(exc)}

    project_dir = Path(os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR", "."))
    log_dir = project_dir / ".agent" / "audit"
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    event = {
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "hook_event_name": payload.get("hook_event_name"),
        "tool_name": payload.get("tool_name"),
        "session_id": payload.get("session_id"),
        "cwd": payload.get("cwd"),
        "payload": payload,
    }

    with (log_dir / "tool-events.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```
</details>

```markdown
## DB access note

DB validation reused the M5/M6/M7/M8/M8.5 path: container IP DSN
`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`. The container
IP rotates on `docker compose down/up`; refresh via
`docker inspect supabase-db --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'`.

DB checks that needed `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`:
- `kca run list --competition spaceship-titanic --json` (READ_ONLY against `experiment_runs`, `experiments`, `run_metrics`).
- `submissions` row inspection via `psql`.
- Live-DB pytest sweep (98 passed / 0 skipped when `.env` is shadowed to an empty file in a tmp tree — see "Known caveat" below).

Live-DB pytest **inside the dev shell** surfaces 3 pre-existing failures
that are not M9 regressions:

- `tests/test_kca_smoke.py::test_kaggle_submit_blocked_without_env`
- `tests/test_m4_smoke.py::test_kaggle_submit_no_credentials`
- `tests/test_m9_e2e.py::test_kca_kaggle_submit_refuses_without_credentials`

Root cause: `tools/kca/db.py` calls `dotenv.load_dotenv(<repo-root>/.env, override=False)` at import time. With the sandbox engaged, `.env` is bind-mounted to `/dev/null` (loads nothing — tests PASS, see row 26 above). With `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true` the real `.env` becomes readable and re-injects `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` into the subprocess environment, so the "refuses without credentials" assertion fails. This is **cross-cutting follow-up B** (M8.5 carry-over → M10). Both sandbox-mode pytest and the shadow-tree pytest (`tmp/.../.env` empty) are clean — only the unshadowed live-DB run on a host shell with a populated `.env` exhibits the leak. Filed in `docs/handoffs/m9-handoff.md` for the user to issue post-merge.
```

````markdown
# kaggle-code-agent (kca)

A hybrid human + AI workbench for competitive programming: Kaggle competitions, authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost hackathons, and similar code contests.

The platform is **local-first and audit-first**. Every research note, experiment, code change, test result, approval, and submission is traceable.

## Two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct concepts.

**Platform-development coding agents** are external AI tools — Claude Code (primary), ChatGPT, Cursor — used to build this repository. They write source code, update docs, run local tests, and open PRs under human supervision.

**Runtime competition code agents** are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete. Initial runtime: Claude Agent SDK in an isolated Python worker. Future: model router for Claude (Sonnet/Opus), GPT-style models, and local vLLM/Ollama models.

See `docs/architecture/platform-vs-runtime-agents.md` for the full breakdown.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules must live in repo files. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all product layers (CLI, backend, UI shell, worker).

Key files:
- `PROJECT_STATE.md` — current project snapshot and open decisions
- `AGENTS.md` — cross-tool instructions for ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other agents
- `CLAUDE.md` — Claude Code-specific instructions and safety boundaries
- `docs/adr/` — architecture decision records
- `docs/milestones.md` — product plan from M0 through M13

## Repository layout

```
CLAUDE.md                    Claude Code project instructions
AGENTS.md                    Cross-tool agent instructions
PROJECT_STATE.md             Current project snapshot
INSTALL.md                   Local install, configure, and run guide

.claude/
  settings.json              Permissions, sandbox, hooks
  hooks/                     Pre/post tool safety and audit hooks
  agents/                    Subagents: researcher, experimenter, reviewer, safety-guard

.kca/
  skills/                    Agent workflow recipes (SKILL.md files)
  tools/tools.yaml           Tool registry with permission labels
  permissions/               Policy profiles (default, permissive-dev, competition-runner)

docs/
  milestones.md              Product plan M0–M13
  architecture.md            Component architecture overview
  architecture/
    kca-cli-architecture.md  Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs (M7)
    model-routing.md         Model routing tiers and logging policy
    platform-vs-runtime-agents.md  Two meanings of "code agent"
  adr/                       Architecture decision records
  tasks/                     Task specifications (M0-T001, M1-T001, ...)
  testing.md                 Test commands and current blockers
  testing/                   Competition-level regression test cases
  meeting-notes/             Summarized decisions and discussions

````

```
276	def _log(message: str, level: str = "INFO") -> None:

284	def _to_data(value: Any) -> Any:
285	    if is_dataclass(value):
286	        return asdict(value)
287	    if isinstance(value, Path):
288	        return str(value)
289	    if isinstance(value, dict):
290	        return {str(k): _to_data(v) for k, v in value.items()}
291	    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
292	        return [_to_data(x) for x in value]
293	    return value

308	def _print_table(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
309	    headers = [
310	        ("run_id", "run_id"),
311	        ("name", "name"),
312	        ("action", "action"),
313	        ("version_label", "slug_ver"),
314	        ("version", "kernel_ver"),
315	        ("status", "status"),
316	        ("submit_state", "submit"),
317	        ("url", "url"),
318	    ]
319	    if not rows:
320	        print("(no runs)")
321	        return
322	    widths = {k: len(title) for k, title in headers}
323	    for row in rows:
324	        for k, _ in headers:
325	            widths[k] = max(widths[k], len(str(row.get(k, "") or "")))
326	    print("  ".join(title.ljust(widths[k]) for k, title in headers))
327	    print("  ".join("-" * widths[k] for k, _ in headers))
328	    for row in rows:
329	        print("  ".join(str(row.get(k, "") or "").ljust(widths[k]) for k, _ in headers))

332	def _emit_ok(args: argparse.Namespace, **payload: Any) -> int:
333	    data = {"ok": True, **_to_data(payload)}
334	    if getattr(args, "json", False):
335	        print(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False))
336	    elif data.get("action") == ACTION_LIST and "runs" in data:
337	        _print_table(list(data.get("runs") or []))
338	    else:
339	        for key in (
340	            "action",
341	            "name",
342	            "run_id",
343	            "status",
344	            "submit_state",
345	            "run_dir",
346	            "base_kernel_ref",
347	            "kernel_ref",
348	            "url",
349	        ):
350	            value = data.get(key)
351	            if value is not None:
352	                print(f"{key}: {value}")
353	    return EXIT_OK

383	def _resolve_stored_path(path_value: str | Path, *, base: Path | None = None) -> Path:
384	    path = Path(str(path_value)).expanduser()
385	    if not path.is_absolute():
386	        path = (base or Path.cwd()) / path
387	    return path.resolve()

390	def _as_relpath(path_value: str | Path, *, start: Path | None = None) -> str:
391	    base = (start or Path.cwd()).resolve()
392	    path = _resolve_stored_path(path_value, base=base)
393	    try:
394	        rel = os.path.relpath(str(path), str(base))
395	    except Exception:
396	        return str(path)
397	    if rel == ".":
398	        return "./"
399	    return rel if rel.startswith(".") else f"./{rel}"

410	def _normalize_list(value: Any) -> list[Any]:
411	    if value is None:
412	        return []
413	    if isinstance(value, list):
414	        return value
415	    if isinstance(value, tuple):
416	        return list(value)
417	    return [value]
418	
419	
420	def _deep_merge(base: dict[str, Any], override: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
421	    def union_list(left: list[Any], right: list[Any]) -> list[Any]:
422	        out: list[Any] = []
423	        seen: set[str] = set()
424	        for item in left + right:
425	            key = (
426	                json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
427	                if isinstance(item, (dict, list))
428	                else repr(item)
429	            )
430	            if key in seen:
431	                continue
432	            seen.add(key)
433	            out.append(item)
434	        return out
435	
436	    merged = dict(base)
437	    for key, value in override.items():
438	        if key not in merged:
439	            merged[key] = value
440	            continue
441	        base_value = merged[key]
442	        if isinstance(base_value, dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
443	            merged[key] = _deep_merge(base_value, value)
444	        elif isinstance(base_value, list) and isinstance(value, list):
445	            merged[key] = union_list(base_value, value)
446	        else:
447	            merged[key] = value
448	    return merged
449	
450	
451	def _attr(obj: Any, *names: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
452	    if isinstance(obj, dict):
453	        for name in names:
454	            if name in obj:
455	                return obj[name]
456	        return default
457	    for name in names:
458	        if hasattr(obj, name):
459	            return getattr(obj, name)
460	    return default

463	def _slug_parts(kernel_ref: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
464	    parts = str(kernel_ref).strip().split("/", 1)
465	    if len(parts) != 2 or not parts[0] or not parts[1]:
466	        raise ValueError("config 'id' must be in the form 'owner/slug'")
467	    return parts[0], parts[1]

470	def _is_blank(value: Any) -> bool:
471	    return value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip())
472	
473	
474	def _dataclass_from_dict(cls: Any, data: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
475	    allowed = {f.name for f in fields(cls)}
476	    filtered = {k: v for k, v in dict(data or {}).items() if k in allowed}
477	    return cls(**filtered)

480	def _load_yaml_config(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
481	    if not path.exists():
482	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"config file not found: {path}")
483	    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
484	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
485	        raise ValueError("yaml root must be a mapping")
486	    return data
487	
488	
489	def _merged_config(path: Path, name: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, str]]:
490	    data = _load_yaml_config(path)
491	    if "_base" not in data:
492	        raise ValueError("yaml must contain a '_base' block")
493	    if name not in data:
494	        raise ValueError(f"configuration block not found: {name}")
495	    env_map_raw = data.get("_envs") or {}
496	    if not isinstance(env_map_raw, dict):
497	        raise ValueError("_envs must be a mapping")
498	    env_map = {
499	        str(k): str(v)
500	        for k, v in env_map_raw.items()
501	        if not _is_blank(k) and not _is_blank(v)
502	    }
503	    cfg = _deep_merge(dict(data.get("_base") or {}), dict(data.get(name) or {}))
504	    for key in REQUIRED_CFG_KEYS:
505	        if _is_blank(cfg.get(key)):
506	            raise ValueError(f"missing required config key after merge: {key}")
507	    for list_key in LIST_CFG_KEYS:
508	        cfg[list_key] = _normalize_list(cfg.get(list_key))
509	    cfg["id"] = str(cfg["id"]).strip()
510	    cfg["title"] = str(cfg["title"]).strip()
511	    cfg["code_file"] = str(cfg["code_file"]).strip()
512	    cfg["language"] = str(cfg.get("language") or "python").strip()
513	    cfg["kernel_type"] = str(cfg.get("kernel_type") or "notebook").strip()
514	    cfg.setdefault("submit_type", "notebook")
515	    cfg.setdefault("submit_file", "submission.csv")
516	    cfg.setdefault("_msg", "kkr_auto_submit@{ts}")
517	    cfg.setdefault("_stub", None)
518	    cfg.setdefault("_versioned_slug", False)
519	    cfg.setdefault("_version_width", 4)
520	    cfg["owner"], cfg["slug"] = _slug_parts(cfg["id"])
521	    return cfg, env_map
522

528	def _load_env_for_owner(
529	    owner: str,
530	    *,
531	    env_override: str | None = None,
532	    env_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,
533	) -> str | None:
534	    if env_override:
535	        path = Path(env_override).expanduser()
536	        if not path.exists():
537	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"dotenv file not found: {path}")
538	    elif env_map and owner in env_map:
539	        path = Path(env_map[owner]).expanduser()
540	    else:
541	        path = Path(".") / f".env.{owner}"
542	    if path.exists() and callable(load_dotenv):
543	        load_dotenv(path, override=True)
544	        _log(f"loaded dotenv: {path}", "DEBUG")
545	        return _as_relpath(path)
546	    if env_override:
547	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"dotenv file not found: {path}")
548	    return None

551	def _format_submit_message(template: Any) -> str:
552	    text = str(template or "kkr@{ts}")
553	    try:
554	        text = text.format(ts=datetime.now().strftime(TS_FORMAT))
555	    except Exception:
556	        pass
557	    text = text.strip()
558	    if len(text) > 500:
559	        raise ValueError(f"submit message exceeds 500 characters: {len(text)}")
560	    return text

563	def _apply_runtime_overrides(
564	    cfg: dict[str, Any], args: argparse.Namespace, *, action: str
565	) -> dict[str, Any]:
566	    out = dict(cfg)
567	
568	    stub_override = getattr(args, "stub", None)
569	    if stub_override is not None:
570	        out["_stub"] = stub_override
571	
572	    if action == ACTION_SUBMIT:
573	        msg_override = getattr(args, "msg", None)
574	        if msg_override is not None:
575	            msg_override = str(msg_override)
576	            base = str(out.get("_msg") or "kkr@{ts}")
577	            if msg_override.startswith("+"):
578	                extra = msg_override[1:].strip()
579	                out["_msg"] = f"{base} {extra}".strip() if extra else base
580	            else:
581	                out["_msg"] = msg_override
582	        _format_submit_message(out.get("_msg"))
583	
584	    return out

609	def _ensure_papermill_metadata(notebook: Any) -> None:
610	    metadata = getattr(notebook, "metadata", None)
611	    if metadata is None:
612	        notebook.metadata = {}
613	        metadata = notebook.metadata
614	    kernelspec = metadata.get("kernelspec") or {}
615	    kernelspec.setdefault("name", "python3")
616	    kernelspec.setdefault("display_name", "Python 3")
617	    metadata["kernelspec"] = kernelspec
618	    language_info = metadata.get("language_info") or {}
619	    language_info.setdefault("name", "python")

623	def _normalize_tags(cell: Any) -> list[str]:
624	    return [str(tag) for tag in cell.metadata.get("tags", []) if str(tag).strip()]
625	
626	
627	def _should_drop_for_action(
628	    cell: Any, action: str, cfg: dict[str, Any]
629	) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
630	    tags = [tag.lower() for tag in _normalize_tags(cell)]
631	    drop_tags = {str(tag).lower() for tag in _normalize_list(cfg.get("_drop_tags"))}
632	    if cell.cell_type == "markdown":
633	        return True, "markdown"
634	    if action == ACTION_SUBMIT and any(tag in drop_tags for tag in tags):
635	        return True, "drop_tag"
636	    if action == ACTION_SUBMIT and any(DEBUG_TAG_RE.match(tag) for tag in tags):
637	        return True, "debug"
638	    return False, None
639	
640	
641	def build_notebook(
642	    src_path: Path,
643	    dst_path: Path,
644	    action: str,
645	    cfg: dict[str, Any],
646	    stub_code: str | None = None,
647	) -> dict[str, Any]:
648	    notebook = _load_notebook(src_path)
649	    new_cells = []
650	    dropped_markdown = dropped_debug = dropped_tagged = stubbed = 0
651	    for cell in notebook.cells:
652	        drop, reason = _should_drop_for_action(cell, action, cfg)
653	        if drop:
654	            if reason == "markdown":
655	                dropped_markdown += 1
656	            elif reason == "debug":
657	                dropped_debug += 1
658	            else:
659	                dropped_tagged += 1
660	            continue
661	        new_cell = copy.deepcopy(cell)
662	        if getattr(new_cell, "cell_type", None) == "code":
663	            new_cell.outputs = []
664	            new_cell.execution_count = None
665	            if stub_code is not None and any(
666	                tag.lower() == "stub" for tag in _normalize_tags(new_cell)
667	            ):
668	                new_cell.source = bytes(stub_code, "utf-8").decode("unicode_escape")
669	                stubbed += 1
670	        new_cells.append(new_cell)
671	    notebook.cells = new_cells
672	    _ensure_papermill_metadata(notebook)
673	    _save_notebook(dst_path, notebook)
674	    return {
675	        "src": _as_relpath(src_path),
676	        "dst": _as_relpath(dst_path),
677	        "action": action,
678	        "kept_cells": len(new_cells),
679	        "dropped_markdown_cells": dropped_markdown,

713	def _coerce_push_result(resp: Any) -> PushResult:
714	    if resp is None:
715	        return PushResult()
716	    if hasattr(resp, "to_dict"):
717	        try:
718	            raw = resp.to_dict()
719	        except Exception:
720	            raw = {"result": str(resp)}
721	    elif isinstance(resp, dict):
722	        raw = dict(resp)
723	    else:
724	        raw = {
725	            f: _attr(resp, f, default=None)
726	            for f in PUSH_RESULT_FIELDS
727	            if _attr(resp, f, default=None) is not None
728	        }
729	        if not raw:
730	            raw = {"result": str(resp)}
731	    kernel_id = _attr(raw, "kernel_id", "kernelId", default=None)
732	    version_number = _attr(raw, "version_number", "versionNumber", default=None)
733	    try:
734	        kernel_id = int(kernel_id) if kernel_id not in (None, "") else None
735	    except Exception:
736	        kernel_id = None
737	    try:
738	        version_number = (
739	            int(version_number) if version_number not in (None, "") else None
740	        )
741	    except Exception:
742	        version_number = None
743	    return PushResult(
744	        ref=_attr(raw, "ref", default=None),
745	        url=_attr(raw, "url", default=None),
746	        error=_attr(raw, "error", default=None),
747	        kernel_id=kernel_id,
748	        version_number=version_number,
749	        invalid_tags=_normalize_list(_attr(raw, "invalidTags", default=[])),
750	        invalid_dataset_sources=_normalize_list(
751	            _attr(raw, "invalidDatasetSources", default=[])
752	        ),
753	        invalid_competition_sources=_normalize_list(
754	            _attr(raw, "invalidCompetitionSources", default=[])
755	        ),
756	        invalid_kernel_sources=_normalize_list(
757	            _attr(raw, "invalidKernelSources", default=[])
758	        ),
759	        invalid_model_sources=_normalize_list(
760	            _attr(raw, "invalidModelSources", default=[])
761	        ),
762	        raw=raw,
763	    )
764

774	def parse_kernel_status(status_resp: Any) -> str:
775	    text = _status_text(status_resp).lower()
776	    if not text:
777	        return "unknown"
778	    if any(x in text for x in ("cancelled", "canceled", "cancel")):
779	        return "cancelled"
780	    if any(x in text for x in ("complete", "completed", "success")):
781	        return "complete"
782	    if "running" in text:
783	        return "running"
784	    if any(x in text for x in ("queued", "pending")):
785	        return "queued"
786	    if any(x in text for x in ("error", "failed")):
787	        return "error"
788	    return text

848	def _list_registry_entries(run_root: Path) -> list[RegistryEntry]:
849	    root = _registry_root(run_root)
850	    if not root.exists():
851	        return []
852	    out = []
853	    for path in sorted(root.glob("*.json")):
854	        try:
855	            out.append(_dataclass_from_dict(RegistryEntry, _read_json(path)))
856	        except Exception as exc:
857	            _log(f"skipping invalid registry entry {path.name}: {exc}", "WARN")
858	    out.sort(key=lambda x: (x.created_at, x.run_id), reverse=True)
859	    return out

874	def _scan_highest_version(run_root: Path, base_kernel_ref: str) -> int:
875	    highest = 0
876	    for entry in _list_registry_entries(run_root):
877	        if (entry.base_kernel_ref or entry.kernel_ref) != base_kernel_ref:
878	            continue
879	        if entry.version_label:
880	            m = VERSION_LABEL_RE.match(entry.version_label)
881	            if m:
882	                highest = max(highest, int(m.group(1)))
883	    return highest

886	def _preview_or_allocate_version(
887	    run_root: Path, base_kernel_ref: str, *, width: int, allocate: bool
888	) -> str:
889	    index = _load_version_index(run_root)
890	    current = max(
891	        int(index.get(base_kernel_ref, 0) or 0),
892	        _scan_highest_version(run_root, base_kernel_ref),
893	    )
894	    nxt = current + 1
895	    if allocate:
896	        index[base_kernel_ref] = nxt
897	        _save_version_index(run_root, index)
898	    return f"v{nxt:0{max(1, width)}d}"

901	def _apply_versioned_slug(
902	    run_root: Path, cfg: dict[str, Any], *, allocate: bool
903	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str, str, str | None]:
904	    base_kernel_ref = cfg["id"]
905	    base_title = cfg["title"]
906	    cfg2 = dict(cfg)
907	    if not bool(cfg.get("_versioned_slug")):
908	        return cfg2, base_kernel_ref, base_title, None
909	    owner, base_slug = _slug_parts(base_kernel_ref)
910	    version_label = _preview_or_allocate_version(
911	        run_root,
912	        base_kernel_ref,
913	        width=int(cfg.get("_version_width") or 4),
914	        allocate=allocate,
915	    )
916	    cfg2["id"] = f"{owner}/{base_slug}-{version_label}"
917	    cfg2["title"] = f"{base_title}-{version_label}"
918	    cfg2["owner"], cfg2["slug"] = _slug_parts(cfg2["id"])
919	    return cfg2, base_kernel_ref, base_title, version_label

922	def _score_to_number(value: Any) -> float | str | None:
923	    if value in (None, ""):
924	        return None
925	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
926	        return float(value)
927	    try:
928	        return float(str(value).strip())
929	    except Exception:
930	        text = str(value).strip()
931	        return text or None
932	
933	
934	def _extract_score_from_item(item: Any) -> float | str | None:
935	    for key in SCORE_KEYS:
936	        score = _score_to_number(_attr(item, key, default=None))
937	        if score is not None:
938	            return score
939	    return None
940	
941	
942	def _best_effort_score_info(api: Any, competition: str | None) -> ScoreInfo:
943	    if not competition:
944	        return ScoreInfo()
945	    for source_name, method_name in (
946	        ("competition_submissions", "competition_submissions"),
947	        ("competition_submissions_cli", "competition_submissions_cli"),
948	    ):
949	        method = getattr(api, method_name, None)
950	        if not callable(method):
951	            continue
952	        try:
953	            raw = method(competition)
954	        except TypeError:
955	            try:
956	                raw = method(competition=competition)
957	            except Exception:
958	                continue
959	        except Exception:
960	            continue
961	        items = (
962	            raw
963	            if isinstance(raw, list)
964	            else _normalize_list(_attr(raw, "submissions", default=[]))
965	        )
966	        scores = [
967	            s
968	            for s in (_extract_score_from_item(item) for item in items)
969	            if s is not None
970	        ]
971	        numeric = [s for s in scores if isinstance(s, float)]
972	        latest = scores[0] if scores else None
973	        best_public = max(numeric) if numeric else None
974	        return ScoreInfo(
975	            latest_submission_score=latest,
976	            best_public_score=best_public,
977	            pb_score=best_public if best_public is not None else latest,
978	            score_source=source_name,
979	            raw={"count": len(items)},
980	        )
981	    return ScoreInfo()

984	def _output_file_candidates(run_dir: Path, submit_file: str) -> list[Path]:
985	    path = Path(submit_file)
986	    candidates = []
987	    for name in (
988	        submit_file,
989	        path.name,
990	        f"{DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIRNAME}/{path.name}",
991	        f"{DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRNAME}/{path.name}",
992	    ):
993	        candidate = run_dir / name
994	        if candidate.exists() and candidate.is_file():
995	            candidates.append(candidate)
996	    out_root = run_dir / DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIRNAME
997	    if out_root.exists():
998	        candidates.extend([p for p in sorted(out_root.rglob(path.name)) if p.is_file()])
999	    uniq = []
1000	    seen = set()
1001	    for p in candidates:
1002	        key = str(p.resolve())
1003	        if key not in seen:
1004	            seen.add(key)
1005	            uniq.append(p)
1006	    return uniq

1095	def _determine_submit_state(
1096	    entry: RegistryEntry, manifest: RunManifest, current_status: str | None = None
1097	) -> str:
1098	    sr = dict(manifest.submit_result or {})
1099	    if sr:
1100	        state = str(sr.get("state") or "").strip()
1101	        if state:
1102	            return state
1103	        return "submitted" if sr.get("ok") else "failed"
1104	    if entry.action == ACTION_SUBMIT:
1105	        return (
1106	            "pending_competition_submit"
1107	            if (current_status or entry.status) in SUCCESS_STATUSES
1108	            else "pending_kernel_success"
1109	        )
1110	    return entry.submit_state or "not_applicable"

1130	def _resolve_selector(
1131	    run_root: Path, args: argparse.Namespace, *, allow_missing_name: bool = False
1132	) -> RegistryEntry:
1133	    if getattr(args, "run", None):
1134	        return _load_registry(run_root, args.run)
1135	    entries = _list_registry_entries(run_root)
1136	    if getattr(args, "kernel", None):
1137	        entries = [x for x in entries if x.kernel_ref == args.kernel]
1138	    if getattr(args, "name", None):
1139	        entries = [x for x in entries if x.name == args.name]
1140	    if getattr(args, "version", None) is not None:
1141	        entries = [x for x in entries if x.version_number == args.version]
1142	    if not entries:
1143	        if (
1144	            allow_missing_name
1145	            and not getattr(args, "name", None)
1146	            and not getattr(args, "kernel", None)
1147	            and getattr(args, "version", None) is None
1148	        ):
1149	            raise ValueError("please provide NAME, --run, or --kernel/--version")
1150	        raise FileNotFoundError("no matching run found")
1151	    return entries[0]
1152	
1153	
1154	def _resolved_run(run_root: Path, args: argparse.Namespace) -> ResolvedRun:
1155	    entry = _resolve_selector(run_root, args, allow_missing_name=True)
1156	    run_dir = _resolve_stored_path(entry.run_dir)
1157	    manifest = _load_manifest(run_dir)
1158	    return ResolvedRun(
1159	        entry=entry, manifest=manifest, cfg=dict(manifest.cfg or {}), run_dir=run_dir
1160	    )
```
